transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (Lumos Head of ML), David Ortiz (Lumos Infra), Priya Singh (PM)

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, this is Alex from Redwood. Quick intros?
00:08 Rachel Kim: Hi Alex, Rachel here, head of ML at Lumos. We're really curious about quantization, we run a mix of NER and long-form summarization, so quality is huge.
00:14 David Ortiz: David, infra. We're concerned about latency and running costs.
00:20 Priya Singh: Priya, product — timeline is Q1 pilot ideally.
00:25 Alex Chen: Great. I'm joined by Maya, our SE, who will walk through Optimize and the INT8/FP8 profiles. We'll show quality vs latency and then talk pilot scope.

02:10 Maya Patel: Alright jumping in — Redwood Optimize recommends quant profiles based on your workload distribution. For NER short context we often see INT8 giving 1-2% quality drop but 2-3x latency improvements. For long summarization FP8 tends to preserve quality better, usually <1% delta, and still gives 1.5x latency gain vs FP16.
02:55 Rachel Kim: When you say quality drop, is that measured by our metrics like F1 for NER or ROUGE for summarization?
03:02 Maya Patel: Yes we use F1/EM for NER and ROUGE/BLEU-ish for summarization. We also run human evals for edge cases. The Optimize tool surfaces a quality-vs-latency curve per profile.

06:15 Alex Chen: Quick note on how we run these — we do a two-stage approach: offline quant profiling with your sample prompts to build candidate profiles, then a live benchmark in a sandbox dedicated pool to measure end-to-end latency including batching and KV cache effects.
06:42 David Ortiz: Does your KV cache get affected by quantization? We rely on long-running KV caches for few-shot.
06:50 Maya Patel: Good question. The KV cache is independent; quantization affects weights and compute kernels, not the cache semantics, though some micro-ops change so latency numbers shift. We call it KV cache, sometimes transcripts show "KV cash" ha.

09:30 Rachel Kim: Any concerns about hallucinations rising with INT8? We saw some drift in values when we tried our own quant pipeline.
09:40 Maya Patel: There can be edge-case regressions, yes. INT8 can increase token-level perplexity which sometimes shows up in hallucinations for very sensitive prompts. That's why Optimize recommends per-prompt regression thresholds and a canary routing — keep critical routes on FP16/FP8 and route noncritical to INT8.

12:05 David Ortiz: On dedicated vs hosted, if we go dedicated for the pilot, can we pin model versions and quant profiles?
12:12 Alex Chen: Yes — Dedicated allows you to pin both model version and quant profile. We also support automated rollbacks if quality regressions exceed your configured thresholds.

15:00 Maya Patel: Demo slide — here is the quality vs latency scatter. (audio: clicking) See the FP8 cluster sits closer to FP16 in quality with modest latency gains; INT8 sits further right with bigger latency gains but wider variance.
15:30 Priya Singh: Can you share the raw numbers for a 2k token summarization?
15:36 Maya Patel: From our public benchmarks: FP16 baseline: 450ms per request on A100-like hardware; FP8: ~300-350ms; INT8: 160-220ms depending on batching. But your throughput and sequence distribution will change those; these are ballpark.

19:10 Rachel Kim: Which hardware are you optimizing kernels for? We use a mix of NVIDIA and Habana in testing.
19:18 Maya Patel: Our runtime supports multiple backends; most kernels are tuned for NVIDIA Ampere/Blackwell GPUs, but we have partners for HPU. For private/on-prem we can bring optimizer builds for your hardware — there is some lead time.

22:05 David Ortiz: Security check — we need SOC2 and customer-managed KMS. Also audit logs and SSO.
22:12 Alex Chen: Yep, Redwood supports SOC 2 compliance, SAML SSO, RBAC, and customer KMS integrations. We'll attach the security pack.

25:40 Maya Patel: Back to quantization — here's a typical rollout strategy: 1) profile offline on samples, 2) run a small canary on dedicated pool with 1-2% traffic, 3) run A/B for 48-72 hours and monitor regression metrics, then 4) increase traffic or fallback to FP16/FP8 if thresholds exceeded.
25:58 Rachel Kim: What metrics should we monitor?
26:02 Maya Patel: Per-route F1/ROUGE changes, token-level perplexity, latency p95, cost per token, and false-positive rates for NER. Optimize can emit alerts on any of these.

29:30 Priya Singh: For the pilot scope, we want a 4-week run: week 1 profiling, week 2 canary, weeks 3-4 wider A/B. Budget wise we want to see at least 30% cost reduction or a clear latency improvement.
29:45 Alex Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose pricing for dedicated pilot and the expected cost numbers in the spreadsheet.

32:00 Rachel Kim: One more on quality — do you store embeddings or any PII in logs during the pilot? We need to maintain data residency.
32:08 Alex Chen: By default hosted retains minimal logs; for pilot on dedicated/private, data never leaves your VPC if you choose private control plane. KMS for key control, and we can turn off request logging or anonymize.

36:10 Maya Patel: Live demo — running INT8 profile on a summarization prompt (audio demo, short pause) ... okay result generated, looks close but slightly terser in details. You can tune temperature and presence to mitigate.
36:55 Rachel Kim: We saw terseness too in our in-house INT8 run. Any config tips?
37:02 Maya Patel: Increase top-p or lower temperature, also use the quality-tuning knob in Optimize which will automatically adjust decoding hyperparams per-profile.

40:30 David Ortiz: For the pilot, we'll need a small dedicated pool. How fast can you provision?
40:37 Alex Chen: We can provision within 48 hours for a standard dedicated pool in hosted regions, longer for private on-prem. We'll include options in the pricing doc.

43:20 Priya Singh: Ok let's recap next steps.
43:25 Alex Chen: Recap: Alex will send pricing and benchmark sheet. Maya will set up pilot run and sample collection. Rachel will share prompts and golden outputs. David will confirm VPC/KMS details. We aim to kick off pilot week of 2026-12-13.

46:10 Rachel Kim: Thanks all, this was helpful.
46:14 Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Tuesday.
46:20 Meeting ended.
